newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat prices steady, old crop maize higher.
newsitem.headline: French wheat prices steady, old crop maize higher.

text.p: French wheat prices were broadly unchanged but demand was driving up old-crop maize prices on Tuesday, dealers said.
"There is demand to cover a few maize deals," one dealer said.
August maize into Bordeaux was quoted at 840 francs per tonne, up five francs on Monday.
But October maize into Bordeaux was bid at 835 francs, down five francs on Monday on prospects of a good 1997 harvest.
Wheat prices reflected expectations that the 1997 crop would show large variations in quality, dealers said.
Standard Rouen wheat with a test weight of 76 kg and a moisture content of 15 percent was quoted at 860-865 francs per tonne for August and at 870 francs per tonne for September-December.
Lower quality wheat was trading at a discount of 10 francs per tonne for each kg missing.
Buyers were offering a premium of five francs per tonne to sellers who could guarantee a minimum test weight of 76 kg.
"But these sellers want at least a premium of 10 francs," one dealer said.

Quality criteria were the focus of negotiations between Iraq and exporters for the import of some 100,000 tonnes of French wheat, with Iraq initially seeking wheat with a test weight of 78 kg, exporters said earlier.

French domestic grains are traded on a July basis, reflecting their underlying value without twice-monthly carrying charges. These must be added to the quoted price for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of June the following year.
